chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood Al-Raqy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Mudabbira (slave woman promised freedom upon her master's death), when her master dies, that her waiting period is four months and ten days from the day her master dies, if her master had copulated with her. It was said to him, 'Supposing the man emancipates his slave girl before his death, by an hour or by a day, then he dies.' He said: 'This one observes the waiting period of three menstruations or three pure periods from the day her master emancipated her.'

key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرَة: A slave woman whose freedom is promised upon the death of her master
key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He copulated with her / had intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a Mudabbira upon her master's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes the iddah of a 'Mudabbira' based on the mode of her transition to freedom: death triggers the longer period of four months and ten days (mirroring widows), while early emancipation by the master requires only three menstrual cycles. Shia jurists utilize this distinction to clarify that the nature of the bond's dissolution—whether by death or manumission—dictates the specific waiting period, ensuring clarity in inheritance and remarriage rights.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood Al Raqy,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Al-Mudabbira (promised freedom upon the death of her master), when her master dies, that her waiting period is of four months and ten (days) from the day of the death of her master, if her master had copulated with her’. It was said to himasws, ‘Supposing the man who emancipates his owned slave girl before his death, by an hour, or by a day, then he dies’. So heasws said: ‘This one would observer the waiting period of three menstruations, or three Quroos (pure periods), from the day her master emancipated her’.
